title: Taiwan Should Be Kept Off the Negotiating Table
gist: Allen Carlson argues the September 2026 Trump-Xi summit, widely read as substance-free, actually marks the clearest sign yet of a major shift in the U.S. position on Taiwan, a shift he attributes solely to Trump. The summit extended the trade truce and touched on AI but agreed little else.

insights.claim: The September 2026 China-U.S. summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping is broadly viewed as having produced nothing of substance beyond extending the bilateral trade truce and discussing artificial intelligence.
insights.speaker: Allen Carlson
insights.so_what: Trade-truce extension keeps tariff escalation risk on hold for now, but absence of broader deals limits upside from a US-China reset.
insights.quote: President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extended their trade truce, talked about artificial intelligence, and agreed on little else.

themes.theme: Hidden shift in U.S. Taiwan policy

insights.claim: Contrary to the consensus that the U.S. position on Taiwan held because Trump did not visibly oblige Xi's push for a policy change, the summit is the clearest sign yet of how far U.S. Taiwan policy has already shifted.
insights.speaker: Allen Carlson
insights.so_what: Markets treating the summit as status quo on Taiwan may be underpricing erosion of U.S. commitment, relevant to cross-strait risk premia and Taiwan-exposed assets such as semiconductors.
insights.quote: What looks like nothing is the clearest sign yet of how far the U.S. position on Taiwan has shifted.

insights.claim: The author attributes the shift in the U.S. stance on Taiwan solely to President Trump rather than to institutional or bipartisan policy evolution.
insights.speaker: Allen Carlson
insights.so_what: If the shift is personal to Trump, it is less durable across administrations but more volatile and transactional while he is in office.
insights.quote: And Trump is solely responsible for such a change.

insights.claim: Xi Jinping used the summit to press Trump to change American policy on Taiwan, signaling Beijing views Taiwan as a negotiable item in bilateral bargaining with Washington.
insights.speaker: Allen Carlson
insights.so_what: The risk of Taiwan being traded within a broader US-China deal is a tail risk for regional security and supply chains.
insights.quote: Xi pressed Trump to shift American policy on the island
